testPolicy.text: UMD is test-optional through the spring and fall 2027 application cycles; students choose whether to submit SAT/ACT scores. CDS C8F: students who do not submit are still considered for admission, limited enrollment programs, living-learning programs and merit scholarships; submitted scores are used in all of these.

cost.totalIncludes: Office of Student Financial Aid, 2026-2027 academic year estimated costs, undergraduate on campus: annual tuition, mandatory fees, on-campus housing with cable and phone 10,290, average food plan 7,180, books and supplies, transportation, personal costs.

inState.note: CDS 2025-26 G1 lists 2026-27 tuition of 10,490 in-state, required fees 1,800 and food and housing 16,747; 23.8% of undergraduates pay more than G1 because of program differentials

aidPromise.text: Terrapin Commitment (since January 2023): UMD's standard in-state tuition and mandatory fees are fully covered for Pell-eligible Maryland residents enrolled full time with unmet need; if scholarships, grants and the student aid index fall below in-state tuition and fees, the grant pays the difference. FAFSA by March 1 each year.

deadlines.early: November 1 (Early Action, non-binding, decision by February 1)

facts.text: For fall 2025, UMD admitted 8,075 of 18,487 Maryland applicants and 22,143 of 48,614 applicants from other states and abroad; 4,133 of the 6,559 enrolled first-years were Marylanders.

Business, computer science, engineering, biological sciences, neuroscience and psychology are Limited Enrollment Programs: admitted students who are not admitted to their LEP major start in Letters and Sciences and must meet gateway requirements to enter it.
The Terrapin Commitment covers standard in-state tuition and mandatory fees for Pell-eligible Maryland residents with unmet need.
89.23% of the fall 2025 enrolled first-years reported a high school GPA of 4.0 or higher, and the average was 4.41.
Applying by the November 1 Early Action deadline gives priority consideration, and the Regular Decision deadline is January 20.

notes: C1 from CDS 2025-26 Excel: applied 33,095 men + 34,006 women = 67,101; admitted 14,151 + 16,067 = 30,218; enrolled 3,163 + 3,396 = 6,559. The residency table fills only the in-state and out-of-state columns (international is blank and evidently included in out-of-state, since the two columns sum to the totals). Waiting list: 247 offered, 0 accepting, 0 admitted as reported. The 2026-27 cost page and CDS G1 differ (tuition 11,014 versus 10,490); the financial aid office figure is used for the totals.
